GLOBAL.take: U.S. integrators are shrinking into profit: UPS lost domestic volume after the Amazon glide-down yet grew adjusted profit 12% on yield, and FedEx grew revenue double digits on price while fuel and trade friction ate its margin. Our read is that the volume they shed is flowing to Amazon's own network, which grew operating income 43% while buying delivery speed, so shippers should expect firm list-rate increases (FedEx +5.9% for 2027) and surcharges from the integrators, and more capable alternatives from marketplace logistics.

companies.name: FedEx
companies.period: Q4 FY2026 (March-May 2026); the June-August 2026 quarter had not been published by 30 September 2026

Post-spin stranded overhead and MD-11 fleet grounding

NA.take: Both North American posts are using price and labour peace to shrink losses rather than to win volume: USPS lifted package revenue 7.7% on 3.4% fewer pieces, while Canada Post's parcel rebound is a recovery from a strike-hit base. In our analysis neither is fixing its balance sheet on its own, so legislative and funding decisions in Washington and Ottawa, not the market, will set how aggressively they can price e-commerce parcels in 2027.

companies.name: USPS (United States Postal Service)
companies.ebit_label: Controllable loss (USPS's own operating measure); net loss $2.5bn
companies.ebit_chg: Improved by $584m YoY (net loss improved by $562m from $3.1bn)
companies.vs_prev: Losses narrowing year on year thanks to pricing, but management still describes a severe liquidity crisis that management action alone cannot fix.
companies.volume: Shipping and Packages volume -3.4% (-55m pieces); First-Class Mail -3.5%; Marketing Mail +4.3%
highlights: Shipping and Packages revenue +7.7% to $8.25bn on price despite lower volume, led by Ground Advantage
Price increases implemented on 26 April 2026; Marketing Mail revenue +12.3%
About 4m work hours removed in the quarter

$15bn statutory debt limit (unchanged since 1992) and unresolved pension and retiree health obligations; about $1.4bn of FERS contributions deferred this quarter
Higher compensation, retirement and fuel-related transportation costs
companies.outlook: No numerical guidance; USPS is asking Congress for legislative relief on debt limit and retirement funding.
companies.exposure: Fuel-related transportation costs add to the pressure, but the main drags remain domestic: falling parcel volumes and the debt limit.

SA.take: Latin American e-commerce volume is concentrating in marketplace-owned logistics: Mercado Libre shipped 45% more items and cut Brazil's free-shipping threshold, accepting a 6.7% operating margin to do so, while Correios and Magalu's e-commerce shrank. Our read is that the state post is becoming a last-resort network funded by the Treasury, and that cross-border shippers into Brazil and Mexico will increasingly need a marketplace or private-carrier route rather than the postal channel.

companies.name: Mercado Libre
companies.revenue_chg: +50% YoY in USD (net revenues and financial income)
companies.vs_prev: Fastest revenue growth in four years and first quarter above $10bn, but margin kept falling as the company funds free shipping, credit and capacity.
